text:
incident-bot: AUTOPAGE fired for service=redwood-serving-canary, release=v3.2.1, reason=canary >5xx threshold (p95 error 12.3%). PagerDuty incident: PD-4821.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: page fired to schedule 'eng-oncall' (PD-4821). Escalation level 1.

maria (oncall): ack

ajay: ack from me too, looking now. any region pinned?

monitoring-bot: Loud signal: canary replicas in us-west-2 showing repeated 502/503s; error-rate spike started ~2m ago tied to model-quant-path. CPU on those pods normal, but token-generation timeouts seen in logs.

sarah: saw this while watching rollout. Canary went to 10% traffic ~5m ago. Metrics: p50 latency +30%, p95 errors up 9->18% for generation endpoints.

javi: confirming logs show repeated `KVCache miss` errors then `RuntimeError: failed to schedule kernel` inside quant path. Posting snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T02:03:10Z] serve-0 gen: ERROR runtime/kernel_scheduler.cpp:142 schedule failed: EAGAIN
[2026-03-15T02:03:11Z] serve-0 gen: ERROR tokenizer: incomplete response, closing stream
```

tom: is this the RLHF quant build we gated? deployment.yml shows image: redwood/serve:v3.2.1-quant.

ajay: yes that image. I'm going to stop canary traffic and scale the canary down to 0 to prevent further customer impact. Doing `rbac route set canary=0` now.

maria (oncall): PD note: I clicked ack in PD, pinged infra oncall. Also adding high-priority tag and sending SMS to rotations.

ops-lead: Good. If rollback needed, coordinate with release owner @sarah. Keep customers informed if SLOs breached.

ajay: command output: ```
> ramp traffic canary=0
Traffic adjustment: canary 10% -> 0% (ok)
> kubectl scale deploy/redwood-canary --replicas=0 -n prod
scaled
```

monitoring-bot: Canary traffic cut to 0. Error rate for stable remains at baseline; aggregate customer-facing errors dropped back to ~1.2%. Canary pods still reporting kernel errors but no traffic hitting them.

javi: recommend rollback of canary image from v3.2.1 to last-known-good v3.2.0 in candidate cluster before we reattempt. I'll prep rollback plan.

sarah: yes please. Also capturing prompt set failures for eval team. We need a regression test entry for quant path.

ajay: starting rollback: `kubectl set image deploy/serve-api redwood/serve:v3.2.0 -n prod` and will monitor.

javi: trying to reproduce locally with the same quant kernel flags; if we can reproduce we'll open a kernel bug with stack trace.

maria (oncall): status update to PD: Canary paged but traffic diverted, impact limited to canary traffic. No global customer pages. PD incident remains open for postmortem.

tom: rollback applied. `kubectl rollout status deploy/serve-api -n prod` shows new pods healthy.

monitoring-bot: After rollback completion: canary error rate stabilized, overall 5xx for generation endpoints back to baseline. No SLO breach on customer-facing metrics.

ajay: I'll keep the canary image at 0 and block any automated re-ramp for 24h. Need a postmortem risk review before reweigh.

javi: created bug RB-873 with logs + kernel traces, assigned to runtime team.

ops-lead: Good triage. Next steps: (1) postmortem with release owner and runtime, (2) patch CI to run quant regression on small prompt set, (3) add guardrail to prevent auto-ramp of images flagged unstable.

maria (oncall): handing off to daytime oncall @tom in 30m. Leaving incident pinned for postmortem notes. If anything changes, wake me.

tom: taking handoff. I'll draft the incident summary and notify support to hold on public status updates until we confirm root cause.

sarah: one more note — customer impact: we saw a handful (~12) of failed generation requests from a single enterprise customer in us-west-2 while canary was at 10%. I'll follow up with account team and include in postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident PD-4821 still open. Autopage resolved (canary cut). Add 'postmortem-needed' label.

maria (oncall): thanks team. closing my active ack, leaving PD incident open for the postmortem.

ajay: closing thread for now; will reopen if any regression reappears.
